title: From Frozen Cinema to AI Dreams: Dustin Yellin's Sculptures Swim to Life in 'Goodnight Lamby'
summary:
Dustin Yellin has always seen his sculptures as "frozen cinema"—elaborate glass blocks layered with painted figures that seem to pause a thousand stories at once. Now, those stories are thawing. In the 15-minute film "Goodnight Lamby," which premiered at the Cannes Classics section this year, Yellin's daughter Zia journeys inside one of his works to rescue her lost stuffed animal. The result is a kaleidoscopic blend of live action, collage animation, and generative AI, produced by Darren Aronofsky's studio Primordial Soup.

The film is a family affair with serious star power. Paul Rudd plays a version of Yellin, while Chris Rock voices a chatty octopus guide. Cinematography comes from Oscar nominee Matthew Libatique, and an acoustic end-credits song by Maggie Rogers sweetens the adventure. But the real technical star is Google Veo 3, a generative AI model that animates elements of Yellin's sculpture "Politics of Eternity." Animators prompted the AI to move isolated elements—rippling water, drifting clouds—against green screens, then composited them digitally. "We got to really dig deep into Dustin's personal aesthetic," said producer Justin A. Gonçalves.

Aronofsky, known for pushing boundaries (and sometimes controversy) with AI, saw this as a chance to wed new tools to genuine artistic vision. Yellin, a self-described "medium agnostic" who works across painting, sculpture, and now film, brushes off criticism of AI-generated art. "You're gonna see so much garbage, but you also see so much garbage in the analog world," he said. "It's not the what you're seeing but the how you're seeing." For him, the tech simply made a decade-long dream possible in months. The plan is to tour the film through museums, letting audiences step inside his once-frozen worlds.
why_it_matters: As AI tools reshape how movies and art are made, a 12-year-old today might one day use similar technology to create stories — but the line between human creativity and machine generation will be a central question of their generation.

background_read: The Cannes Film Festival, held annually in France, is one of the world's most prestigious film events, where 'Goodnight Lamby' premiered in its Cannes Classics section dedicated to heritage cinema.
Darren Aronofsky is a director known for intense psychological films like 'Black Swan' and 'Requiem for a Dream'; his production company Primordial Soup supported the experimental use of AI here.
Google Veo 3 is a generative video model that turns text prompts and still images into moving footage, part of a recent wave of AI tools stirring debate in Hollywood.
Yellin's signature works are large glass blocks with painted figures trapped between layers, creating what he calls 'frozen cinema' — now literally brought to life through digital compositing.
The film's end-credits song comes from Maggie Rogers, a singer-songwriter whose folk-pop style often blends acoustic instruments with modern production.

perspectives.description: Artists like Yellin can realize decade-long visions in months, democratizing high-end animation that once required huge budgets. AI becomes a collaborator that amplifies personal expression rather than replacing it.

Critics warn that generative AI could flood the culture with low-effort content, devalue human craft, and lead studios to replace animators and designers. The technology risks undermining the very labor that made Yellin's original sculptures possible.

Every new art technology, from photography to digital editing, was first called 'not real art.' The shock usually fades once the tool becomes part of the creative palette, but each shift does permanently change who gets to make art and how audiences judge it.

Museum tours of AI-infused works may become a new genre, but ethical guidelines around crediting AI contributions and paying original artists whose work trains the models remain unresolved. The 'how you see' may increasingly depend on legal contracts as much as artistic vision.
